No verifications yet. Every provider round seeds forecasts at +1, +3, +6, +12 and +24 hours and judges them once that hour has passed, against the median of the analyses: come back after a few hours of use, the ranking builds itself.

Every round seeds forecasts and judges them against the median of the providers\' analyses (quorum of three): no single judge. Weights are learned per variable and horizon band; below the threshold the macro-region priors rule, and no provider ever drops below the floor. The \"use only this\" override applies where the provider reaches: where it does not cover, the cascade takes the wheel back.
Override active: only %1$s where it reaches.
No verifications on this window yet.
Mean error |p − outcome|: 0 is perfect, 0.5 is guessing. Providers speak by the hour: their probability over the window is the maximum of the hourly ones, the weather-app convention.

Here the phone barometer and the providers answer the same question — does it rain in the window? — and are judged with the same yardstick (|probability − outcome|). The first verifications arrive after a few hours of use.

The share is the learned weight (1/(MAE+0.3)², MAE decayed with a 14-day half-life) normalised among those with verifications, averaged over the variables: it is the same maths that drives the fusion.

Recalibrated = the model\'s probability mapped onto the true frequency of your verifications (Platt scaling). Analogues = among the most similar pressure situations in your archive, how many ended in rain; they weigh N/(N+40).

Activity recognition tells the engine when you are in a car, on a bike or on the move: those readings are discarded before they become a false weather change. Without it, the engine relies on GPS altitude alone.
A lift is not a front

A ten-minute burst at one reading per second starts now: its median, compared with the services\' sea-level pressure, estimates your sensor\'s bias. No need to stay here. Then the engine needs about thirteen hours of history before its first verdict: the bar on the home tells you how far along it is.
